patch_description: Instead of blind random-walk simulated annealing that moves arbitrary points (wasting moves on points that don't affect the bottleneck), this approach: (1) uses barycentric coordinates for exact, clean feasibility projection into the equilateral triangle, (2) targets perturbations only at points participating in the currently smallest triangle — the active constraint — which is the key efficiency gain, (3) runs a short multi-start over several structurally diverse seeds (vertex+edge-heavy, hexagonal-ring rotated 30°, and perturbed-lattice) with two-stage screening, and (4) uses an adaptive step schedule with restarts from the incumbent. This concentrates search effort where the objective is actually determined, escaping lattice-seeded local basins and yielding far larger minimum areas.
